PASS: PASS (round 1). Audited HEAD b7ddba8, working tree clean. Sprint 25 diff = f296262..HEAD
(8a9d263 findings, b7ddba8 code; 94127b7 is start bookkeeping).

SPRINT FILE: re-read fresh immediately before this verdict. The only change since
Master Controller's f296262 is the lifecycle-owned status: todo -> in_progress line.
No requirement amended. No A->B "arrives between versions" criterion in this sprint.

REQUIREMENTS
R1 met. docs/sprint-25-database-outage-findings.md holds five verbatim JSON
recordings (prod healthy / paused / restored, local DNS failure, local connection
refused), supabase-js 2.112.3 (matches the installed package), date 27 Sep 2026, the
measurement script source, the paused-state /api/health/db response (503, down), and
the pre-fix 404 observed live. Raw data, not a paraphrase. It also states plainly what
was NOT observed (a fetch timeout), which is the right thing to put on record. The anon
key is omitted from the curl example; I checked, and no secret is in the doc.
R2 met. One classifier, lib/supabase/availability.ts: error present, status 0, empty
code. Imported by all three call sites (reading page, horoscope action, chart save).
grep for message.includes / "fetch failed" / ENOTFOUND in app/ and lib/ returns
nothing outside tests. Fixtures are parsed out of the findings doc's own json blocks at
test time, so they cannot drift from the recording. Covered: paused (RPC and insert),
DNS, refused, 22P02, empty result, and 23502. The first test asserts the recording
count, so silently dropping a block from the doc fails the suite.
R3/R4 traced in page.tsx. Only the classifier's true verdict throws
DatabaseUnavailableError. Malformed id (22P02, status 400), missing id (null error,
empty data), and any other RPC error still fall through to the unchanged
`if (error || !data || data.length === 0) notFound()`. The thrown error's message is a
fixed string, and error.tsx reads no params and renders no error text, so nothing in
the unavailable output is derived from the id. The route has no loading.tsx and no
Suspense and no generateMetadata, so there is no early flush and no second RPC that
could 404 first. That is the static half of "the 5xx survives rendering". The real
status code is LiveQA's to prove with curl -i, as the sprint says.
R5 met. The classifier picks the message. A 23502 keeps "Save failed, try again."
(covered by a recorded fixture). The redirect still carries the date, so the cast chart
re-renders beside the error.
R6 met. app/chart/page.tsx is untouched. No database call is added to the /chart GET path.
R7 met. The action throws into the same error boundary instead of redirecting to a
page that 404s. The non-outage load failure keeps its existing redirect.
R8 met. console.error on all three unavailable paths. The reading page's notFound path
still logs nothing. The chart save's non-outage insert failure keeps the Sprint 18 R6
log it already had, which is not a 404 path.
R9 met. lib/llm/, app/api/, app/components/, ReadingPanel.tsx, app/chart/page.tsx,
layout, globals.css and package*.json are all absent from the diff. generate.test.ts
passes unmodified.

CI steps (all green locally): lint clean, typecheck clean, test 195/195 across 20
files (7 new), build compiled. Every CSS variable in unavailable.module.css already
exists. No new tokens, no new dependency.

NON-BLOCKING (low), for Dev Team or Master Controller to decide, not a condition:
app/reading/[id]/error.tsx is a route-wide error boundary, so it catches every
exception on /reading/[id], not only DatabaseUnavailableError. A render bug (say,
composeChart throwing on bad stored positions) now shows "The service behind saved
readings isn't responding." That is a false outage claim to the visitor. Its docblock
says the copy "is true for both". The heading and "try again in a few minutes" are
true for both; the service-not-responding sentence is not. Operators still see the real
error in the server log and still get a 500, so nothing is hidden from us, only
mislabelled to the visitor. The cheap fix is to drop the causal sentence and keep the
rest, which still satisfies R3. I have not reproduced this, so it is a note, not a FAIL.

No test named known-failing or pre-existing. No new Human Prerequisites: the sprint's
own pause/restore prerequisite already covers LiveQA's pass.

Handoff: Dev Team runs /sprint-dev-done 25. LiveQA owns what a static read cannot
prove: the real 5xx status via curl -i while paused, that both 404 cases still 404
while paused and after restore, and the action's error boundary in a real browser.
